To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) SVMs and random forests are the most accurate methods, followed closely by boosted trees, neural nets, and bagged trees; 2) SVMs are the most accurate when the data set is linearly separable, but random forests are the second most accurate method in all other cases; 3) boosted stumps are the fastest methods, followed closely and surprisingly by naive bayes and logistic regression; 4) boosted stumps and naive bayes are the least accurate methods
SVMs and neural nets perform best on average, but that boosted trees perform the best on the hardest tasks.

SVMs, boosted trees, boosted stumps, random forests, bagged trees and naive Bayes are the most accurate methods, that SVMs and boosted trees are the best at minimizing the 0-1 loss, and that SVMs and random forests are the best at maximizing the area under the ROC curve.
